rubriker.title: 2026 Us Chess Championships Round 9
US Championships: So wins again, now a full point ahead
rubriker._rss_content: Wesley So defeated Andy Woodward in round eight of the US Championship to extend his lead to a full point over Fabiano Caruana, who drew against Sam Sevian. The two will meet in Monday's ninth round. In the women's tournament, Alice Lee and Rachael Li remain tied for first place on 6/8, while Thalia Cervantes moved within half a point of the leaders by defeating four-time national champion Carissa Yip. | Photo: Lennart Ootes / Saint Louis Chess Club

rubriker.title: 2026 European Chess Club Cup Round 3
European Club Cup: Favourites set for direct encounters
rubriker._rss_content: Eleven teams remain tied for first place in the open section of the European Club Cup after three rounds, with tenth seeds Beer Sheva the only top-twelve team to have dropped a match point. The fourth round will see SuperChess facing Bayegan Pendik, with a potential battle between Anish Giri and Nodirbek Abdusattorov (pictured) on the top board. In the women's competition, Monte-Carlo and Gambit Bonnevoie are the only teams with perfect scores and will meet on Tuesday. | Photo: Gerd Densing

rubriker.title: The hour of the seconds
rubriker._rss_content: The World Championship match between Gukesh Dommaraju and Javokhir Sindarov is approaching. The contest gets underway on 24 November in Cologny, near Geneva. Who will be helping the two contenders this time? Sindarov will be able to count on the assistance of his compatriot Abdusattorov, among others, as Abdusattorov himself recently revealed. | Photo: UzChess / Yoav Nis

rubriker.title: Comienza la batalla de los analistas
rubriker._rss_content: Se acerca el match por el Campeonato Mundial de Ajedrez entre Gukesh Dommaraju y Javokhir Sindarov. El enfrentamiento comenzará el 24 de noviembre en una localidad cercana a la ciudad suiza de Ginebra. ¿Quiénes ayudarán a los dos contendientes en esta ocasión? Sindarov podrá contar, entre otros, con el apoyo de su compatriota Abdusattorov, tal como este último reveló recientemente. | Foto: UzChess / Yoav Nis

rubriker.title: From quitting chess to becoming a Grandmaster - Interview with Arturs Neiksans
rubriker._rss_content: GM Arturs Neiksans looks back on his remarkable chess journey, from growing up in the small Latvian town of Valka and discovering chess at age nine to representing Latvia and eventually becoming a Grandmaster. He explains why he stepped away from competitive chess, how a career detour ultimately brought him back to the game, and how coaching, streaming and commentary became increasingly important parts of his life.

rubriker.title: European Club Cup: Crowded at the top
rubriker._rss_content: A total of 108 teams are competing in the European Club Cup in Budva in the open section, with 22 in the women's competition. On paper, the favourites in the open are Bayegan Pendik Chess Sports Club from Turkey, with an average Elo rating of 2715. Bayegan are also the only team with an average rating of 2700 or higher, although four other teams - Alkaloid, SuperChess Romania, Novy Bor and Tuxena - have averages of at least 2600. These five teams are also among the 25 in Budva that have won both their matches in the first two rounds. | Pictured: Alkaloid's Wei Yi | Photo: Gerd Densing

rubriker.title: Total Chess proposes unified rating system
rubriker._rss_content: Total Chess has proposed a new rating system that combines players' classical, rapid and blitz ratings into a single figure. Developed by researcher Mehmet Mars Seven in collaboration with Norway Chess, the formula uses existing FIDE ratings to assess overall playing strength across the three formats. Magnus Carlsen (pictured) tops the inaugural ranking, followed by Hikaru Nakamura and Nodirbek Abdusattorov. The system will undergo testing and public consultation before potential revisions. | Photo: Nils Rohde / ChessBase

rubriker.title: La Asamblea General de la FIDE prepara cambios en la normativa de partidas clásicas a ritmo más acelerado
rubriker._rss_content: La FIDE está preparando cambios en la normativa que regula los ritmos de juego clásico más cortos, tras una resolución de la Asamblea General basada en una propuesta de la Federación Islandesa de Ajedrez. El Consejo de la FIDE tiene previsto establecer el ritmo de 60+30 como un control de tiempo estándar para el ajedrez clásico, sin necesidad de autorización especial, mientras estudia ampliar el uso del ritmo de 45+30. Se mantendrían las restricciones sobre el número de partidas por día y las normas para la obtención de títulos, y se realizarán nuevas consultas antes de tomar decisiones sobre modificaciones más amplias en el reglamento de los torneos de ajedrez clásico. | Foto: FIDE
